newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Petrogal asks Portugal to seek delay EU diesel law.
newsitem.headline: Petrogal asks Portugal to seek delay EU diesel law.

text.p: State oil company Petrogal has asked the Portuguese government to request a delay of up to one year in implementing a European Union law which reduces sulphur levels in diesel, while it upgrades its refineries for the changes, a spokesman said.
"The reason for the request of a delay up to a maximum of one year is that we need the time to upgrade our refineries," Antonio Mocho told Reuters.
He said Petrogal expected to receive a reply from the office of Secretary of State for Energy Jose Penedos later on Friday.

Mocho said the sulphurisation units at its 210,000 barrels per day (bpd) refinery in Sines in southwestern Portugal should be ready by April 1997 and at its refinery in Matosinhos in the north by October 1997.
The new EU law, due to be implemented on October 1, means all diesel fuel must contain a maximum 0.05 percent sulphur, down from 0.2 percent now.

Royal Dutch/Shell's Portuguese retail subsidiary expects to start distributing Petrogal's low sulphur diesel in Portugal from April next year when the sulphurisation units at the Sines refinery should be ready, a Shell spokesman said.
"The majority of our stocks are from Petrogal, so we have to supply to Petrogal's specifications," Miguel Carmo Vaz told Reuters.
"As soon as the sulphurisation units are working, the low sulphur diesel will have to be supplied to everyone."
Officials at the office of the Secretary of State for Energy were not immediately available.
